reasons: [reasoning_validity/major] D1 [alternatives[4] 'Negotiate the lease'; alternatives[3] 'Lease 48 months, then buy a successor'] The month-48 purchase-option threshold is wrong. The draft says an option priced below about $94,490 PV (about $130k nominal, 94,490/0.72692) would make leasing competitive. But K16's $94,490 is the PV budget for all lease-side costs in months 49-72, and that budget includes service. If the lab exercised a purchase option at month 48, it would still pay $1,500/month service for months 49-72: 1,500 x (a72 - a48) = 1,500 x 16.0727, about $24,109 PV. So the option price must be below about 94,490 - 24,109 = $70,381 PV, which is about $96,820 nominal at month 48. That matches the K9 resale breakeven, as it should. The draft's $130k figure overstates the price at which a negotiated option makes leasing competitive by about $33k nominal, and a CFO could use it as a negotiating target. The 'lease then buy a successor' alternative has the same omission ('PV below about $94,490 plus any resale credit' leaves out the successor's service costs).

The verdict text was not changed, and it still presents the discount-rate flip in one direction only ('It reverses ... if the right discount rate is below about 7.53% per year'). [minor/reviewer] D2 [criteriaAssessments C4 assessment and weaknesses; CL12; remainingUncertainty[4]] The new risk-adjusted-residual counterpoint is left purely qualitative ('net effect is not quantified'), but a one-line illustration is easy and would help the CFO. For example, discounting the $90k residual at 12%/12 gives v48 of about 0.6203, so the residual's PV falls from about $65.4k to about $55.8k and the lease's 48-month edge grows by about $9.6k. That is about twice the base gap. Without a number, the reader cannot tell whether this effect outweighs the borrowing-rate effect it is set against.

[minor/reviewer] D3 [alternatives[3] 'Lease 48 months, then buy a successor at month 48'] The revised 'Lease 48 months, then buy a successor' text mixes valuation bases. It gives the threshold as '$70,381 PV ... or about $96,821 paid at month 48, plus any resale credit'. The resale credit is a month-72 amount, so adding it to a month-48 nominal figure needs it converted to a month-48 value. The text also credits the successor's year-6 resale without netting the year-6 resale the buy-and-keep path would get for the old unit (K16 assumes R = 0 for buy-and-keep). The extra credit should be the difference between the two resale values, not the successor's whole resale.
